In this teahouse, must jasmine itself and Brew 5 always taste the same?

She grafts medlar onto damson and sets the result aside as Graft 1; then she grafts mulberry onto medlar and calls the result Graft 2; then she grafts Graft 1 onto Graft 2 and calls that Graft 3; then she grafts medlar onto Graft 3 and sets the result aside as Graft 4; then she grafts Graft 4 onto mulberry and calls the result Graft 5.

However she chooses her four starting cuttings, quince itself and Graft 5 always grow into exactly the same plant. That is simply how this orchard works, without exception.

One spring her neighbor wonders about something. Take any four cuttings — again call the first quince, the second medlar, the third damson, and the fourth mulberry. Graft medlar onto damson and set the result aside as Graft 1; then graft Graft 1 onto damson and call the result Graft 2; then graft damson onto mulberry and call that Graft 3; then graft Graft 2 onto Graft 3 and set the result aside as Graft 4; then graft medlar onto Graft 4 and call the result Graft 5.

In this orchard, must quince itself and Graft 5 always grow into the same plant?
